name: Bold Custom Pricing
summary: Shopify wholesale and B2B pricing app by Bold: separate prices for tagged customer groups, VIP and member tiers, quantity breaks and tiered pricing on one storefront, without Shopify Plus.
best_for: Shopify stores that want to sell wholesale, B2B or VIP prices from their existing storefront without Shopify Plus, with quantity breaks and one or a few customer groups
skip_if: you cannot afford wrong prices at checkout during setup and have no staging theme to test on; you need more than one price list on a $29 budget; or you sell wholesale through Shopify POS and do not want the $129 plan
honest_knock: Bold Custom Pricing has no free plan and charges by customer group: a second price list already takes you from $29 to $69 a month, and bulk CSV pricing and the Shopify POS integration sit only on Complete at $129. The reviews are split more sharply than the 4.4 suggests, with 58 of 538 at one star. The recent complaints are specific: price syncing that broke and 'wreaked havoc' (October 2026, fixed by support), crashes for three weeks with no answer from support (June 2026), incorrect pricing that cost more than the app (February 2026), a slower store and order numbers disturbed while support removed the app (February 2026), and ten days of changing cart quantities and wrong prices after migrating to the new version (April 2025). We have not run the app ourselves; this dossier is read from the listing and its reviews.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Essential · per month, pricing for 1 customer group
pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-11-26 on apps.shopify.com/customer-pricing: every plan name and amount unchanged; first read 2026-10-06 on the Shopify App Store listing at apps.shopify.com/customer-pricing, where the app is titled Custom Pricing: Wholesale B2B; prices in USD) Three plans, each with a 14-day free trial, and the ladder is built on how many customer groups can see their own prices. Essential is $29 a month for 1 customer group, with storewide or product and variant discounts, unlimited quantity breaks, a customisable quantity-break grid, tax controls and manual customer tagging. Standard is $69 a month for up to 10 customer groups and adds automatic tagging by country or purchase history with an automatic email when a customer is tagged. Complete is $129 a month for unlimited customer groups and adds advanced pricing rules, bulk CSV price import and export, the Shopify POS integration, premier support, expert setup and a service level agreement. There is no free plan. All charges are billed in USD, and recurring and usage-based charges are billed every 30 days.

schema_offer.description: Essential, pricing for 1 customer group; Standard $69 for up to 10 groups, Complete $129 for unlimited groups; 14-day free trial; billed every 30 days. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-26.

compare_with.name: Wholesale Gorilla
compare_with.why: Wholesale Gorilla is in our dossiers too. Read on 19 September 2026, it costs $34.95, $69.95 or $149.95 a month with a 21-day trial and no free plan, and it does not meter customer price groups: pricing rules and groups are unlimited on all three tiers, so you climb for features rather than volume. Bold Custom Pricing does the reverse and sells groups: 1 for $29, 10 for $69, unlimited for $129. A store with a single trade tier pays less on Bold; a store with several trade tiers on a small budget gets more groups for its money on Wholesale Gorilla's $34.95 Lite, provided its features cover the rest. Bold's own case is its wider family of apps (Memberships, Bundles, Discounts, Multi-Currency) and a launch in 2013.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Bold Custom Pricing (in the admin BOLD Custom Pricing: Wholesale) on a Shopify development store: the install, a forced plan choice, the Essential test charge approved without a payment method, one wholesale price rule of 20 percent for one product made in about 2 minutes after the plan approval (the sync stayed in the queue, so the price was not seen in the store), the three plans shown in the app and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was billed. Install: the install button of the App Store listing was pressed at about 14:40 in our own tab; Shopify showed the Install app dialog with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved. The app first showed an onboarding screen with Book my onboarding (a free session with an expert) and Continue without help; we chose Continue without help and booked nothing. The app then forced a plan choice (Select Your Account Plan) before the dashboard opened. In the admin the app is called BOLD Custom Pricing: Wholesale, while the App Store title is Custom Pricing: Wholesale B2B. Plans and approval: the plan screen shows Essential - $29 billed monthly (14-day free trial, 1 Customer Tag, Manual Customer Tagging, Tax Controls, Unlimited Quantity Breaks), Standard - $65 billed monthly (Most popular; 1-10 Customer Tags, Auto-Emails, Auto-Tagging) and Complete - $129 billed monthly (Unlimited Customer Tags, Advanced Detailed Pricing, CSV Price Imports, Shopify POS Integration, Expert Setup, Premier Support, SLA). The dossier names Standard at $69, while the app shows $65. We chose Essential, the cheapest; a dialog Update Plan said This change will update your plan to: Essential at $29 / month. Shopify then showed an Approve subscription screen: You will not be billed for this test charge., plan Essential, $29,00 USD every 30 days, You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., Total $29,00 Due 1 Dec, with an Add payment method row that was not filled in. Because the screen said it was a test charge, we approved it; no payment method was entered and nothing was billed, and the app opened without a further payment question. Core action, one price rule for wholesale customers, about 2 minutes after the plan was approved (saved at about 14:42) and about 12 screens or clicks: Manage Tags, Add Tag with the tag wholesale and Discount % 20 (the description is required and the form said Description cannot be empty. until we typed Trade customers); then Product Pricing Groups, Create Product Pricing Group with the Internal Name Wholesale 20 percent off, Calculation Type Percent Discount, Select Products and The 3p Fulfilled Snowboard ($2629.95); Setup Pricing showed a column wholesale with 20 %, and Save. A first try with an empty group had been thrown away because the first group screen said You must have at least one price level for your group. until the tag existed. Result: the group list shows Wholesale 20 percent off, switched on, with Sync queued, and a notice Syncing 0 items with Shopify, 1 items in queue with Product prices will not be updated until its process is synced: and the label In Queue. After 10 seconds it still said In Queue. We did NOT see the price in the store or in the theme preview for a tagged customer, because the sync was still queued; the effect of the rule on a store page was not tested. The onboarding checklist (Select a theme, completed 0 of 5, with a remark about a password protected store) was not followed, because that would ask for a theme change. Cancelling: no payment was ever due, so there was no paid subscription to cancel, and no cancel step was looked for inside the app. The app was uninstalled via Settings, Apps, the row BOLD Custom Pricing: Wholesale and Uninstall; the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason is required, we gave Testing multiple apps, and Shopify confirmed that the app was uninstalled. No call or demo was booked. Not tested: the price on the storefront for a tagged customer, checkout, POS, quantity breaks, Auto-Tagging (Standard), CSV import (Complete), a second group or tag, the theme selection and preview, and the onboarding session. Clean up: no theme changes were saved; the app was uninstalled, which removes its tag and group; other apps were not touched; our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app forces a plan choice before the dashboard, a tag with a description has to exist before a group can be saved, the price rule stayed in a sync queue so the result could not be seen, and the Standard plan costs $65 in the app against $69 in the dossier.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Bold Custom Pricing (in the admin BOLD Custom Pricing: Wholesale) on a Shopify development store: the install, a forced plan choice, the Essential test charge approved without a payment method, one wholesale price rule of 20 percent for one product made in about 2 minutes after the plan approval (the sync stayed in the queue, so the price was not seen in the store), the three plans shown in the app and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was billed. Install: the install button of the App Store listing was pressed at about 14:40 in our own tab; Shopify showed the Install app dialog with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved. The app first showed an onboarding screen with Book my onboarding (a free session with an expert) and Continue without help; we chose Continue without help and booked nothing. The app then forced a plan choice (Select Your Account Plan) before the dashboard opened. In the admin the app is called BOLD Custom Pricing: Wholesale, while the App Store title is Custom Pricing: Wholesale B2B. Plans and approval: the plan screen shows Essential - $29 billed monthly (14-day free trial, 1 Customer Tag, Manual Customer Tagging, Tax Controls, Unlimited Quantity Breaks), Standard - $65 billed monthly (Most popular; 1-10 Customer Tags, Auto-Emails, Auto-Tagging) and Complete - $129 billed monthly (Unlimited Customer Tags, Advanced Detailed Pricing, CSV Price Imports, Shopify POS Integration, Expert Setup, Premier Support, SLA). The dossier names Standard at $69, while the app shows $65. We chose Essential, the cheapest; a dialog Update Plan said This change will update your plan to: Essential at $29 / month. Shopify then showed an Approve subscription screen: You will not be billed for this test charge., plan Essential, $29,00 USD every 30 days, You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., Total $29,00 Due 1 Dec, with an Add payment method row that was not filled in. Because the screen said it was a test charge, we approved it; no payment method was entered and nothing was billed, and the app opened without a further payment question. Core action, one price rule for wholesale customers, about 2 minutes after the plan was approved (saved at about 14:42) and about 12 screens or clicks: Manage Tags, Add Tag with the tag wholesale and Discount % 20 (the description is required and the form said Description cannot be empty. until we typed Trade customers); then Product Pricing Groups, Create Product Pricing Group with the Internal Name Wholesale 20 percent off, Calculation Type Percent Discount, Select Products and The 3p Fulfilled Snowboard ($2629.95); Setup Pricing showed a column wholesale with 20 %, and Save. A first try with an empty group had been thrown away because the first group screen said You must have at least one price level for your group. until the tag existed. Result: the group list shows Wholesale 20 percent off, switched on, with Sync queued, and a notice Syncing 0 items with Shopify, 1 items in queue with Product prices will not be updated until its process is synced: and the label In Queue. After 10 seconds it still said In Queue. We did NOT see the price in the store or in the theme preview for a tagged customer, because the sync was still queued; the effect of the rule on a store page was not tested. The onboarding checklist (Select a theme, completed 0 of 5, with a remark about a password protected store) was not followed, because that would ask for a theme change. Cancelling: no payment was ever due, so there was no paid subscription to cancel, and no cancel step was looked for inside the app. The app was uninstalled via Settings, Apps, the row BOLD Custom Pricing: Wholesale and Uninstall; the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason is required, we gave Testing multiple apps, and Shopify confirmed that the app was uninstalled. No call or demo was booked. Not tested: the price on the storefront for a tagged customer, checkout, POS, quantity breaks, Auto-Tagging (Standard), CSV import (Complete), a second group or tag, the theme selection and preview, and the onboarding session. Clean up: no theme changes were saved; the app was uninstalled, which removes its tag and group; other apps were not touched; our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app forces a plan choice before the dashboard, a tag with a description has to exist before a group can be saved, the price rule stayed in a sync queue so the result could not be seen, and the Standard plan costs $65 in the app against $69 in the dossier.
